A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BrepLLM and Brep2Text, and their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. All supplied pages were inspected, including v2's Appendix A. V1 references an appendix but contains none.

before.justification: V1 reports original Brep2Text captioning and classification results in Tables 1–2, qualitative examples, and component/training ablations in Tables 4–7.

after.justification: V2 reports original captioning, classification, and ablation results in Tables 1–5, plus dataset analyses and additional qualitative comparisons and dialogues in Appendix A.

M1.justification: V2 removes the residual Mixture-of-Query Experts component and its third fine-tuning stage, replacing v1's three-stage adaptation with two-stage MLP/LoRA alignment. The backbone changes from Phi-2 to Qwen3-8B. Adaptive sampling, the hierarchical BrepEncoder, and CLIP-style pretraining remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use Text2CAD-derived Brep2Text with abstract/beginner questions for CAD captioning and generative classification. V2 expands examples within these existing tasks, including dialogue already illustrated in v1; it adds no distinct benchmark or documented controlled test scenario.

E2.justification: V2 Tables 1–2 add LLaVA-13B and Qwen3-VL-8B alongside the retained PointLLM, ShapeLLM, and MiniGPT-3D baselines, substantially broadening comparison to image-based models. Appendix Table 12 also expands the qualitative comparator set beyond v1's MiniGPT-3D-only comparison.

E3.justification: Reported settings change substantially: BrepLLM grows from 2.9B to 8.4B parameters, face/edge sampling bounds change from [16,32] to [32,64], and the main-text judge changes from Qwen-Max to Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507. Image-baseline evaluation is added. Appendix A.2 still names Qwen-Max in places, leaving the evaluator documentation inconsistent.

E4.justification: V1's three-stage ablations and MQE timing study become two-stage studies in v2, including a Stage-II-only control and removal of the MQE analysis. Appendix A adds question/answer-length and vocabulary analyses, expanded qualitative comparisons, and additional dialogue cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for performance. V2's new dataset histograms describe corpus composition rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 replace headline results: classification average changes from 57.05% to 60.0%, captioning judge score from 58.89 under Qwen-Max to 61.36 under Qwen3-30B, and human precision from 81.85 to 83.62. Ablation values, several baseline values, and qualitative outputs also change. These are results under revised model/evaluator settings, not controlled same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Removing MQE also removes v1 Section 3.3's mathematical definition of residual composition, Qfinal = Qbase + Qresidual. The sampling, feature-concatenation, and contrastive-learning definitions in Equations 1–7 remain mathematically unchanged; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list withdraw the residual-MQE/three-stage alignment contribution and redefine adaptation around two-stage transfer of 2D priors with LoRA. The central claims of native B-rep understanding, the Brep2Text benchmark, and leading captioning/classification performance remain.

C2.justification: V2 removes the explanation of late-stage MQE specialization and early-routing noise. Its sampling discussion emphasizes continued importance after full training, whereas v1 stresses diminishing dependence. Appendix A.4 newly interprets dialogue examples as evidence of occlusion robustness and hidden-geometry understanding, without a controlled robustness study.

D1.justification: V2 supplies dataset-generation and evaluator prompts, detailed fine-tuning learning-rate/warmup schedules and iteration counts, and TinyGPT-V initialization information absent from supplied v1. Reported hardware changes from one to four 80GB A800 GPUs, and a project-page link is added. Conflicting evaluator names limit reproducibility clarity.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reframed around procedural CAD, direct B-rep learning, and 3D language models. V2 adds discussion of SolidGen, BrepGen, NeuroNURBS, DTGBrepGen, HoLa, AutoBrep, and BrepARG, among others. It also explicitly attributes 2D-prior transfer and MQE to MiniGPT-3D and emphasizes construction-history data constraints.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites related work and substantial portions of the introduction, experimental narrative, and conclusion. It reverses the order of qualitative results and ablations, adds a structured appendix, and revises the title, author list, and B-rep terminology. These changes exceed simple renumbering or added results.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, replaces the introductory dialogue illustration, revises the architecture diagram, and restructures comparison and ablation tables. New appendix displays include dataset histograms, word clouds, prompt tables, an expanded qualitative table, and dialogue panels; the encoder diagram is substantially retained.

improvement.justification: Image-based baselines strengthen comparison coverage, while Appendix A supplies previously missing prompts and fine-tuning details, improving transparency and reproducibility. These benefits are limited by conflicting evaluator names and unclear ablation reporting: Tables 3–5 label 61.36% as accuracy, while classification Table 2 reports 60.0%. The larger backbone and changed judge also prevent interpreting higher scores as a controlled methodological improvement.
